title: OpenPlate — choose the visual world
question: Four phone mockups of the same Day Board (Tuesday: breakfast and lunch logged, dinner open). Keep the rolled direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Crate Label
options.thesis: Every meal is printed as its own seed packet: bold litho ink, illustrated food, and four food-group bands along the bottom.
options.viewport: A cobalt sunburst sky with a slab 'Tuesday', a stack of packets, a red LOG stamp, and a week rack of seven mini packets.
options.risk: Food illustrations need real production; as rough SVG they look like clip art.

raised.raise: Fixed-scale registration: every packet in the week rack is drawn at the same size and position, so days compare at a glance.
Food entries are a ruled list with honest quantities set flush right (~2 fists).
Month history is a packed grid of stamp-sized packets, not a chart.
One live control: the portion picker rescales the packet illustration as you drag it.

options.label: Thali Table
options.lineage: steel thali and bento: the divided plate seen from above
options.thesis: The balanced plate is literal: a steel thali whose four bowls fill as each food group shows up.
options.viewport: Today's big thali at the top, meal rows below as small thalis, and a week of steel dots.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: round bowls can read like progress rings or calorie donuts if not handled carefully.

options.label: Food Lines
options.thesis: Each food group is a coloured line running through the day; meals are stations where lines stop or pass through.
options.viewport: Four vertical lines, meals as interchange stations, and the week as a route of seven stops.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: 'protein passed through without a stop' explains balance better than any ring. Loses on audience: home cooks don't think in metro maps.
options.risk: Gets complicated with many snacks; needs strict diagram rules.

options.label: Plate Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase day names cropped at the edge, meals as flat colour tiles, and the coach as a live tile.
options.viewport: 'tuesday' at poster size with the next day peeking in, tiles for meals and actions, a lime coach tile.
options.case: Very clear and fast to operate; loses on audience fit, since it reads as a 2012 phone OS rather than food.
options.risk: Reads as retro Windows Phone; little food warmth.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.viewport: Fixed-scale plates of the week on one baseline.
options.case: Lands on cream paper and italic serif, the incumbent look you want to leave.
options.risk: Too close to the old Sage & Cream design.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.viewport: Day as side A / side B tracklists.
options.case: Fixed tape length implies a budget to fill, which turns into calorie counting.
options.kept: Ruled list with quantities flush right.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.viewport: Packed grid of hundreds of thumbnails.
options.case: Too dense for a quick daily log; no audience connection.
options.kept: History as a packed stamp grid.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Type play has nothing to say about food balance.
options.kept: One live control remapping the whole visual.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean nutrition tracker: white cards, rounded meal rows, soft green accent, food photos.
canonCard.viewport: Today header, meal cards with photos, a floating add button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from MyFitnessPal / Cal AI by design.
